title: Suffices to a two-claim valuation package for Putnam 2025 A6
intent: Reduce the main theorem's single-index valuation goal at k to a stronger package of two claims that hold for every j ≥ 1 (the valuations of b(2^j) and of A b (2^j) - 1), so that the two interdependent claims can be proved once by simultaneous induction and the case k recovered by instantiation and padicValInt.mul.

parent.name: putnam_2025_a6
parent.statement:
theorem putnam_2025_a6 (b : ℕ → ℤ)
  (hb0 : b 0 = 0)
  (hb : ∀ n, b (n + 1) = 2 * b n ^ 2 + b n + 1)
  (k : ℕ)
  (hk : k ≥ 1):
  padicValInt 2 (b (2 ^ (k + 1)) - 2 * b (2 ^ k)) = 2 * k + 2

children.name: h (the strengthened valuation package)
children.statement: (∀ j ≥ 1, padicValInt 2 (b (2^j)) = j + 1) ∧ (∀ j ≥ 1, padicValInt 2 (A b (2^j) - 1) = j + 1)
children.closed_by: hP proved by Nat.le_induction (lines 1432-1581) with base cases base_case_b/base_case_A (line 1436) and a succ step carrying both halves of the IH together (obtain ⟨ih_b, ih_A⟩ := ih, line 1439); then constructor with two projections (lines 1583-1585) recovers the two conjuncts of h

applicability.goal_shape: A goal fixed at a single index k (here padicValInt 2 (b (2^(k+1)) - 2*b(2^k)) = 2*k+2) whose proof needs the same valuation property at every index j ≥ 1.
applicability.use_when: the natural statement is a universal claim over indices (∀ j ≥ 1) that strengthens the single-index goal, and two such claims are mutually dependent so they must be proved together by one induction.
applicability.avoid_when: the strengthened statement is false or harder to prove than the original; the reduction from the package back to the goal is not routine (here it still needs the error-term analysis at lines 1033-1426); or the strengthened claim should be a reusable standalone lemma rather than an inline suffices.

claims.claim: Assuming the package h, the reduction derives hv_prod : padicValInt 2 (b (2^k) * (A b (2^k) - 1)) = 2*k+2 in three lines (1029-1031) by padicValInt.mul and ring, after instantiating the two conjuncts at j := k (lines 1022-1023).
claims.evidence: https://github.com/project-numina/Numina-Putnam2025/blob/60d33c8ba19af905bd731e938ebde1c5b8c76519/NuminaPutnam2025/putnam_2025_a6.lean#L1018-L1031; the file is built by the project's CI, .github/workflows/lean_action_ci.yml running leanprover/lean-action@v1 (lake build) on push and pull_request

claims.claim: The package h is closed by simultaneous induction: hP (line 1432) is proved by Nat.le_induction (line 1434) with base cases base_case_b and base_case_A (line 1436), and the closing constructor with two projections (lines 1583-1585) recovers the two conjuncts of h.
The authors state why the two claims are bundled into one suffices package: 'The key is that these claims are interdependent and must be proven together' (lines 1428-1429).

The suffices step separates a short reduction from a long induction: the reduction from the package to the parent is 14 lines (1018-1031) while the induction that proves the package is 154 lines (1432-1585).

consequences: Creates one new obligation (the package h) plus the reduction obligation in the suffices' `by` block (that h implies the parent). The strengthened statement quantifies over all j ≥ 1, so it must hold at every index, not just k; a false strengthened claim makes the whole proof unprovable. The two conjuncts are coupled: each induction step of hP uses both halves of the IH (obtain ⟨ih_b, ih_A⟩ := ih, line 1439), so they cannot be split into two independent inductions. A too-strong suffices is a silent dead-end: it fails only when the package goal is attacked.
